title: Does a smaller turn bring the windmill back?
description: A paper windmill with four equal blades looks the same after a turn of ninety degrees about its red centre point. A smaller turn leaves every blade short of the next blade place, so the windmill looks different. Keeko's doubt is that a turn of forty five degrees also brings it back.
teaching_notes: One idea: the smallest turn that brings a figure back onto itself is the gap from one equal part to the next. Watch for students who think any turn that moves the blades a little will do.

video_script.why: The child sees that a turn smaller than the gap between two blades leaves each blade short of the next blade place, so the windmill looks different.
video_script.substitution: Turn the windmill by a small angle and check whether each blade lands on a blade place.
video_script.anchor: a paper windmill with four equal blades and a red point at its centre

video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says a turn of forty five degrees also brings the windmill back. After that turn each blade stops halfway between two blade places, so the windmill looks different. Only a turn of ninety degrees puts each blade on the next one.
video_script.payoff_line: The windmill does not look the same for a turn smaller than ninety degrees

final_answer.value: No, the windmill does not look the same for a turn smaller than a quarter turn
final_answer.spoken: the windmill does not look the same for a turn smaller than ninety degrees

maths_rules: A turn after which a figure looks exactly the same is called an angle of symmetry
4 equal blades share a full turn of 360 degrees, so the gap from one blade to the next is 360 / 4 = 90 degrees
A turn of 45 degrees is half of 90 degrees, so each blade stops halfway between two blade places
Any turn smaller than 90 degrees leaves each blade short of the next blade place, so the windmill looks different
The first turn that makes the windmill look the same is 90 degrees
video_script.design: One idea: a turn smaller than the gap between two blades cannot bring the windmill back. The windmill stays on the board all video. Wrong idea: a turn of forty five degrees also works.
